principles.text: Set stops around 1-2% regardless of setup or entry tactic; usually at the low of day, sometimes at the bar low or just below the anchor VWAP.
Selling into strength is never wrong; if undecided, flip a coin to pick trim-vs-hold, then review after the trade to gradually build your own selling approach.
In a strong uptrend it's the perfect time to be aggressive and buy as much as you can, because you don't know how long the market will last; rather be too bullish than try to pick the top.

Treat the current AI move like the 1998-2000 dot-com analog: NASDAQ ~15% above the 150 EMA is early (the run extended to ~26-28% above before topping); don't short too early, and prepare for an eventual large correction afterward.

Getting shaken out of winners after red candles is the most common mistake; you only need to successfully hold one big winner through the pullbacks to learn to sit through them — it's a gradual process, not perfection.
Too many external opinions (e.g. Twitter) deteriorate trading; protect your own internal process — even re-watch mentor streams a day later to avoid being influenced in real time.
